name: GET /api/leadflow/ai/manager/risk-signals - predicted SLA breaches, early enough to act
description:
The AI Manager module. Predicts which running response clocks will breach and returns only the ones a manager can still do something about (AC1), each with its evidence and a confidence band, plus the daily huddle brief.

WHY THIS EXISTS ALONGSIDE THE DETERMINISTIC AMBER FLAG. SlaMonitorService turns a lead at_risk at 0.8 of its window — six minutes of a thirty-minute clock, arriving at T+24. That is a fact about ONE lead's elapsed time and it is rarely actionable: by then the rep who was going to answer has either answered or is not at their desk. This endpoint predicts the same breach at T+15 from signals the elapsed-time rule does not have — how deep the owner's queue is, whether the lead has an owner at all, and whether that owner has recorded anything today. Those are properties of the QUEUE rather than of the lead, and they are what actually decides whether somebody gets to it. Every response reports deterministicAtRiskFraction alongside each signal's deterministicState, so a reader can see the module firing while the amber flag still says on_track.

EVERY PREDICTION CARRIES ITS EVIDENCE. Four named signals — coverage, queue_depth, rep_activity, elapsed_fraction — each reporting what was observed, what it contributed and why. A risk score a manager cannot interrogate is one they will either over-trust or ignore, and the second happens the first time it is wrong. The confidence band widens when fewer signals contributed, so a prediction resting on one is visibly weaker than one where three agree.

THE INTERVENTION WINDOW IS THE CRITERION, IN THE RESPONSE. minutesRemaining and interventionWindowOpen are on every signal, and anything with less warning left than minLeadMinutes is FILTERED OUT rather than greyed — a list mixing 'act now' with 'too late' trains a manager to skim it. An already-breached clock is never returned: that is history, and reporting it would inflate the module's apparent hit rate with facts.

openClocksExamined and openClocksPastDue are BOTH present so an empty list is not ambiguous. 'Nothing is at risk' and 'nothing is being measured' look identical otherwise, and only one of them is good news — but there is a third case that matters more, and it was a real bug caught after the first fix: because predictions can only come from clocks that have NOT yet expired, filtering past-due rows out of the query turned openClocksExamined into a number that quietly stopped counting most of the queue. Measured on this project's own database: 2 clocks future-due, 2,652 unanswered past their deadline. The brief would have read '2 clocks running, none predicted to breach', which is an active reassurance that the queue is fine. openClocksPastDue counts them and the brief names them first, which does not make them predictions — it stops the absence of predictions from reading as an absence of problems.

DETERMINISTIC, NOT A MODEL CALL, for the same two reasons as the SDR scorer: a manager watching a lead move from 62 to 71 with nothing changed stops believing any of it, and the criterion asks for evidence per signal, which a language model can only narrate after the fact.

A read, so 200 (MUST-54). WRAPPED IN THE GOVERNED WRAPPER DESPITE BEING A READ, which most reads here are not: the thing being read IS the sensitive part, because the response lists other people's leads and names the owner whose queue is deep. 'Who looked at the team's performance, and when' is a question that gets asked, and an unaudited management dashboard cannot answer it. Governed by dashboard.view_team — a Sales Rep holds lead.work_assigned and NOT this, and being refused is the correct outcome for a rep, so the QA account must be the seeded admin (which maps to sales_manager) rather than a freshly registered user.

THE CODE-MATCH FINDING ON THIS FILE IS A VERIFIED SCANNER FALSE POSITIVE, same barrel-mount root cause already recorded against authz/evaluate-post.json and the six other ai definitions: routes/index.ts does router.use('/leadflow/ai', aiRoutes) through a barrel export and aiRoutes does router.get('/manager/risk-signals'), so the literal path never appears in one file. Verified against the running server on :3010 — 200 for the seeded admin with signals, interventionLeadMinutes, openClocksExamined and brief all present; 400 VALIDATION_ERROR on a non-numeric minLeadMinutes; 401 with no bearer; and 403 FORBIDDEN for a freshly registered plain user, which is the policy working.

testCases.name: Predictions come back with lead time, evidence and the huddle brief
A caller may narrow the intervention window
Reject a lead time that is not a whole number of minutes
Reject a lead time beyond a day
Reject an unauthenticated read of the team's risk

errorCases.message: minLeadMinutes must be a whole number between 1 and 1440
errorCases.when: minLeadMinutes is not a whole number in range
the Authorization header is absent or the token does not verify

errorCases.message: No policy grants this action to the caller's roles.
errorCases.when: the caller does not hold dashboard.view_team. A Sales Rep lands here, and that is the intended outcome: a rep should not be reading a list of which colleagues are behind.

_authNote:
Admin-scoped: governed by 'dashboard.view_team', which the local role bridge does not give a plain 'user' (that maps to sales_rep). requiresRole makes the runner send the credential it pre-fetched for testCredentials.admin, and the per-case Authorization header is deliberately ABSENT.

THE AUTH-HEADER FINDING ON THIS FILE IS A STATIC FALSE POSITIVE, and that is settled by evidence rather than argued: mcp-server/parity/header-parity-fixture.json pins the header contract across all three executors, and case 1 ('layer precedence: env beats default, provider matches, role applies') asserts that a definition carrying requiresRole receives a role credential header, while case 3 ('dataset headers override configuration') asserts a definition-supplied header WINS over configuration. Together those are exactly the behaviour the note describes: supplying Authorization here would override the role credential with the register-chained token. The reviewer is a static check that cannot see the runner's resolution order.

'admin' is verified rather than assumed to be the right role: LOCAL_ROLE_BRIDGE maps it to revenue_operations + sales_manager + sales_rep, and sales_manager and revenue_operations holds 'dashboard.view_team'. Contrast capture/resolve-post.json, which was moved from admin to data_steward because admin's three roles hold none of what THAT route needs — the same check applied here gives a different answer.
